headline: Geometry-aware models extend molecular, glycan, and complex structure prediction
label: Biomolecular Structure Prediction Models
summary: Recent preprints and papers from July 2026 pair 3D geometric and surface representations with diffusion and equivariant networks for biomolecular tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of explicit geometric structure in learned representations of biomolecules. SenCos-GEM encodes 3D molecular geometry with a law-of-cosines consistency loss and SE/FiLM adapters, and MolMAE pretrains a surface-guided masked autoencoder on ~261K bioactive molecules using surface point clouds, 3D graphs, and fragment information. FUSED describes ligand binding sites by jointly combining structural CDPA covariance descriptors with elemental ilr-coordinate descriptors. SweetFold adapts the Boltz-1x all-atom diffusion model to glycan, glycoprotein, and protein-glycan complex structures. On the assessment side, ORIGAMI applies an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network to estimate interface iLDDT for multimeric complexes, while LINKER predicts residue-functional group interactions from protein sequence and ligand SMILES. The new element across these items is the incorporation of geometric constraints and symmetry into the representation or model, as in the law-of-cosines loss and SO(3) equivariance. The evidence here consists of preprint and early published abstracts.
